Love the content, but I respectfully disagree here. Measuring productivity gains isn’t about the individual, the human is the 10%, while the AI provides the 100%. Just because your close knit business wouldn't replace a valued employee doesn't mean most white collar jobs aren't vulnerable over the next few years. This shift is likely inevitable and unstoppable, but the world on the other side will look vastly different. Soon, even in your field, video creators will simply pick a topic, and AI will handle the rest of the preparation, reducing production time to 1% of what it is now. Creators who stick to manual workflows will be competing against thousands of channels releasing equal or better content in a fraction of the time. In a fixed attention economy, slower creators will see their views drop. In the past, human intelligence built tools that moved our labor up the value chain. But when the tool itself is intelligence, human labor becomes redundant

I think there is an important distinction between traditional automation and what AI may become capable of. Historically, automation has often replaced specific tasks while increasing productivity, creating new industries, and sometimes even increasing the number of jobs overall. But AI feels different because it is not only automating physical labour or narrow repetitive tasks. It has the potential to automate cognitive work, creative work, administrative work, analysis, communication, coding, design, decision-making, and eventually even management functions. When combined with rapid advances in robotics, the line between “tool that helps a worker” and “system that replaces the worker entirely” becomes much thinner. So while past automation often changed jobs rather than eliminating the need for humans altogether, AI and robotics could potentially move us toward complete automation in many areas. If AGI eventually arrives, it could eliminate or drastically reduce the need for human labour across a huge number of roles. That does not mean it will happen overnight, but I think it is reasonable to say this wave of automation may not follow the same pattern as previous ones.
